bluf: Impression is an independent Nottingham performance marketing agency, founded 2012, 120+ people, with London, Manchester and New York offices, that leads with SEO and sells GEO, paid search, paid social, programmatic, CRO, digital PR and measurement under an Evidence into Action approach. The record shows it building the AI search line on proof: the Tensar GEO case claims 1,793 AI Overview citations and 47,604 clicks, and it publishes an llms.txt. A rival should know that four of six tested lines are contradicted by its own house (no Google ads, no LinkedIn ads, no social pixel, no testing tool), and that Clarins and Funky Pigeon already buy from other tracked agencies.
doing:
The positioning line, an independent performance marketing agency that uses a proven experimentation process and proprietary tools to turn evidence into action for ambitious brands, decodes as a full channel performance shop whose differentiator is testing discipline rather than any one channel. The headline claim, quoted as a claim, is a Performance Marketing Agency of the Year title, awarding body not shown in the capture, and GEO work for Tensar earning 1,793 AI Overview citations.

SEO alone scores 3: site schema lists it first, a five item SEO nav cluster includes GEO, and the homepage leads with the Tensar case. Seven core lines score 2: AI Search / GEO (Tensar, 1,793 citations and 47,604 clicks), CRO (Lotus Car Rental and And So To Bed cases), Content & Digital PR (EnviroBuild, And So To Bed and Marmalade), Data & Measurement (media measurement, data stack and GMP nav items; a Norse incrementality case), Paid Search (Wizz Air AI bidding and Cancer Research UK PPC), Paid Social (Cornish Company and a Snapchat campaign for a humanitarian charity) and Programmatic & CTV (weather triggered DOOH for Norse Atlantic). Partners: Google Partner and Google Marketing Platform. Proprietary: Alexis and Velocity, in house technology by nav label, and the Evidence into Action approach. Local and Web & Product score 0.

AI posture in plain terms: GEO sold on the Tensar case, AI bidding applied in paid media (a 36% cut in cost per flight search for Wizz Air), and an AI at Impression page in the nav; the move read marks P1 partial because no audited AI visibility product shows. Pricing signals: none. Recent moves: none dated, no news, no jobs; the sitemap holds 95 case study URLs with lastmod dates from 2025-09-10 to 2026-01-23 (the £3.5m humanitarian donation campaign). Conspicuously absent for a performance agency: any ads of its own in either library, and any social pixel or testing tool on its own site.
clients:
The Radar files Impression's clients as mixed, its home market the UK (Nottingham, London, Manchester) plus a New York office. Verticals: Ecommerce & retail, B2B & manufacturing, SaaS, Fintech, Sustainable brands, Travel & airlines, Charity and Insurance.

The needs read counts 16 clients from 2 case studies and 14 slugs: 12 observed and 4 names only. AI and automation leads the mix at 0.225 on Tensar (GEO that 'secures 47,000+ clicks in a year'), Wizz Air ('36% reduction in cost per flight search' via AI bidding; also coded paid and organic) and Norse Atlantic Airways, whose 'Traffic Campaign Case Study' title names no AI. Paid performance, 0.176, adds Topps Tiles ('Paid Media') and Rutland Cycling (slug 'paid media'). Stanhope Insurance came for organic demand ('21% increase in organic conversions'), Marmalade and EnviroBuild for PR ('Digital PR', '900+ placements'), And So To Bed and Lotus Car Rental for CRO, coded web build from 'cro' slugs, Clarins for brand ('flagship product launch') and The Access Group for B2B and brand, though its title reports '32% traffic increase'.

The names only are Cancer Research UK (titled with name and 2023 only; a capability note cites PPC), Funky Pigeon and hVIVO (no title) and Queensmith, uncoded though its title claims a 114% revenue uplift; needs inferred from the SEO led mix.

Two clients shop: Clarins also sits with labelium, Funky Pigeon with found.

Horus places Impression best for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers): it is likely, moderate confidence, that Tensar, Wizz Air and Norse Atlantic Airways ask next for audited citation share, which P1 partial says it does not yet sell. Under KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out), its SEO and paid hours have a roughly even chance of repricing first.
house: Say and do: 2 of 6 tested lines practised on its own house. AI Search / GEO is corroborated: it publishes an llms.txt listing key pages for language models, with 3 AI topic URLs in the sitemap and no AI crawlers blocked. Publishing cadence is corroborated: the sitemap lists 548 URLs, 41 updated in 90 days and 66 in 365 days. Paid Search is contradicted: no Google ads of its own, Transparency Center status none, count 0. LinkedIn advertising is contradicted: no LinkedIn ads of its own, while 725 ads match the name query across all advertisers. Paid Social is contradicted: no social ad pixel on its own site. CRO is contradicted: no testing tool detected on its own homepage. Meta and TikTok status is not recorded. The tag stack is gtm alone, on WordPress and Nuxt, with no pixels, test tools or ABM stack. Social links: LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, X and Facebook.
market:
The Horus read scores Impression 9.2 on the tailwind index, 44th percentile, band Neutral, sold mix at 16:55 on the Solar Arc, dusk (Atum), resilience 31.8. Best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), carried by AI Search / GEO and Content & Digital PR, and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers scale faster than any channel before them), carried by Paid Search and AI Search / GEO. Most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out), driven by SEO, Paid Search and Paid Social, and KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two). Best fit: The Toll Road, 36/100. Moves: P2, P4 making; P1, P7 partial; P6, P8 absent; P5 unknown; P3 not applicable.

Monsoon: 49.3, Breeze, 26th percentile, migration 47.8 against displacement 50.8. The verdict says 48 of the index is the sold mix, SEO (12) and Paid Search (6) carrying the most movable hours; shore 65% South and Southeast Asia, 20% Eastern Europe, 15% Africa. Footprint inferred, no hub offices; onshore claims are the in house technology labels Alexis and Velocity.
openings:
The strongest opening is the house against the pitch: an agency selling experimentation and evidence has no testing tool on its own homepage, no social pixel, no Google ads and no LinkedIn ads of its own. A rival whose own house passes those four tests can very likely lead with them in any pitch that mentions Evidence into Action (moderate confidence: a Nuxt front end may hide tags). Falsifier: a testing tool, a social pixel or its own library ads at the next compile.

It sells GEO on one strong case with no audited AI visibility product, so a rival leading with a citation share number across the book likely wins the AI search conversation. No ads tested inside AI assistants show, so the first agency in its segment with results there sets the price. No public pricing model exists, so an outcome priced offer is a conversation it cannot have in public. Its KJ6 exposure rests on SEO, paid search and paid social hours, the lines its house does not practise; Clarins and Funky Pigeon already shop. Monsoon reads Breeze with displacement 50.8, so price is a lever with part of the book only.
watch: Indicator I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, next reading late October 2026: growth above 15% with AI Mode ads live would confirm S1 and strengthen KJ1, where the Tensar GEO line is best placed.

Indicator I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, next reading late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.
Indicator I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the next milestone ($2B) and pricing below $20 CPM bear on KJ2 and on the assistant ad tests P8 says it is not yet making.
Indicator I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: outcome pricing at a top five holdco would deepen KJ6, its main exposure.

The dated move to follow up is the 2026-01-22 Tensar GEO case; the next Radar compile after 2026-09-28 refreshes ads, sitemap cadence and clients, and its own ads appearing in either library would retire two of the four contradictions.
